Root-Cause Hypothesis: RTP and manual scan may use different definition versions, archive handling, exclusions, or verdict normalization. The screenshots do not establish which path is responsible.

Example Scenario to Validate: In an isolated VM, scan the same inert EICAR test file after a definition update: first on write via RTP, then on demand from the identical path and hash.

Expected vs. Reported Behavior: Expected: both scan paths use the same definition generation and return a consistent detection/quarantine result. Reported: a sample was called clean in a manual scan while RTP reportedly detected it; reproduce before assigning root cause.
author: Admin

text: Root-Cause Hypothesis: Protected-resource ACLs, service access controls, or kernel enforcement may be absent or insufficient for the tested account and installation state. Example Scenario to Validate: On a disposable, authorized test VM, attempt a rename and write to a signed product binary as a standard user and as an elevated administrator; capture the exact access result and product logs. Expected vs. Reported Behavior: Expected: unauthorized mutation is denied and audited while supported update/repair flows remain functional. Reported: AV files could reportedly be renamed or modified; the privilege level and exact file are not documented.
author: Admin

text: Root-Cause Hypothesis: Category taxonomy, wildcard/apex matching, allow/deny precedence, or policy cache refresh may be inconsistent across browser, DNS, and encrypted traffic paths. Example Scenario to Validate: In a controlled test profile, classify a documented chat-domain test set, add one domain to the allowlist, apply the policy without reboot, and test apex plus subdomain variants over HTTPS. Expected vs. Reported Behavior: Expected: the chat category and explicit allowlist produce deterministic, documented precedence across supported traffic paths. Reported: WhatsApp categorization/allowlisting failed and a restricted chat site remained accessible.
author: Admin

text: Root-Cause Hypothesis: Category feed coverage, refresh cadence, domain normalization, and keyword-rule scope may vary; the estimate is user-reported rather than a measured benchmark. Example Scenario to Validate: Build a dated, legally approved QA corpus with expected categories; test parent domains, subdomains, redirects, and a fresh taxonomy sync, recording false positives and false negatives. Expected vs. Reported Behavior: Expected: documented category coverage is versioned and repeatable, with block/allow outcomes matching the test corpus. Reported: only 20–40% coverage on a tested category, while explicit blacklist tests were positive.
author: Admin

text: Root-Cause Hypothesis: Selection state may be lost in bulk restore, quarantine metadata may not sync to exclusions, or UI/service calls may fail without isolated error handling. These are separate repro candidates. Example Scenario to Validate: Quarantine two harmless test files, restore only one, verify the other stays quarantined, then restart the UI and recheck exceptions. Separately exercise add-folder and delete flows with permission denial and interrupted service responses. Expected vs. Reported Behavior: Expected: only the selected item is restored, exception state persists, and failures surface without a crash. Reported: bulk restore, missing exception, add-folder crash, delete failure, and assessment mismatch require independent confirmation.
author: Admin
